answer: Membership descends from a single lineage, and each seat may sponsor just one child before its own line closes. When a seat is spent twice, both branches must double the posted bond, their children double it again, so a fan-shaped family of k clones owes roughly k-squared in total security. Honest agents walk a straight line and pay the base bond once. An opal seal on every seat marks its parent, a cedar post records each split, and a lantern audit simply walks the tree, so hidden farms glow because their branches multiply the pledge while abandoning a branch forfeits it.
